title: SMART: High-Performance SAR ATR Through Model-Architecture Co-Design on FPGA
problem: SAR ATR systems suffer from high latency, large memory footprint, and high power consumption, particularly in resource-constrained environments like small satellites.
motivation: Real-time, energy-efficient SAR ATR is critical for remote-sensing image recognition in satellite and edge computing systems.
method: Develops a compact CNN with integrated spatial, channel, and cross attention mechanisms using softmax-free attention and quantization. Implements a customized FPGA accelerator with streaming dataflow architecture using HLS on Xilinx Alveo U280, featuring parameterized hardware kernels for key operations to optimize dataflow.
key_novelty: Model-architecture co-design combining softmax-free attention mechanisms with FPGA streaming dataflow architecture for SAR ATR systems.
contributions: Compact CNN with integrated spatial, channel, and cross attention mechanisms with softmax-free attention approach
Customized FPGA accelerator with streaming dataflow architecture using HLS
29× lower latency and 66× higher energy efficiency compared to CPU/GPU implementations
Superior accuracy on MSTAR (99.84%), SynthWakeSAR (94.85%), and GBSAR (99.92%) datasets
primary_theme: Co-designed CNN and FPGA architecture for efficient SAR target recognition
